text:
Anders Lee spent 923 games and most of a decade as the face of the Islanders, captain included. Now he's 36 and in Utah, playing a little under 14 minutes a night, and the move has given him a different job: depth forward on a team with young stars ahead of him.

He's doing the job well, the scoreboard just hasn't noticed. Utah gets 63% of the expected goals at five on five with Lee on the ice, ten points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him among the best play drivers in the league last season once teammates and competition were accounted for, though they also noted his results ran well ahead of his chances.

This year it's the reverse. He has three goals on 8.4 expected, shooting under 6%, and the team has scored 6.2 fewer goals than expected with him out there. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows he still lives at the net front (91st percentile for chances from the home-plate area) and sets up an unusual share of plays from behind the net. Goals tend to follow chances like these. Watch the finishing turn before you write off the age.
headline: Lee is driving play in Utah, just not scoring
